newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac urges Juppe to put on weight.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac urges Juppe to put on weight.

text.p: In an novel explanation of his deep unpopularity, French Prime Minister Alain Juppe revealed on Friday that President Jacques Chirac had told him people would find him more likeable if he put on weight.

The balding premier has been venting his spleen at being unloved in an extraordinary series of interviews to promote a book "Entre Nous" (Between Ourselves) in which he admits to feeling wounded by constant criticism.
"Being tall and thin doesn't make you friendlier, you know," Juppe told Radio Luxembourg in his latest confession.
"The president often tells me "You ought to put on 10 kilos (22 lbs), people would find you more cuddly'. He's probably right," Juppe said.

Asked if he was jealous of rotund political rivals such as National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin or former interior minister Charles Pasqua, Juppe replied: "Honestly no. Not at all. I feel much better in my own skin."
A local newspaper meanwhile reported on Friday it had found a Bordeaux woman whose insult in the street Juppe said prompted his book.
The woman, identified by the daily Sud-Ouest only as Marie, confirmed she had shouted "Death to idiots" as Juppe walked by and made clear she had no regrets.
"I'm not sure I would enjoy talking to him. I'm not sure I'd manage to go the distance. But I would enjoy explaining to him where he's going wrong. Perhaps I'll take up writing too," she said.

Opinion pollsters say Juppe is unpopular more because of his centre-right government's austerity policies than for his personality. Voters find him dry, arrogant and insensitive, but they also find him courageous and determined.
